articles.title: Past experiences with classical music predict a taste for sophisticated genres
articles.summary: A newly developed scale finds that emotional experiences with classical music during childhood predict a preference for sophisticated genres like jazz and opera later in youth.

articles.title: The genetic influences on drinking may shift between adolescence and early adulthood
articles.summary: At age 17, drinking was linked to genetic predispositions for sensation seeking. By age 23, it was linked to genetic predispositions for alcohol consumption itself, according to a study of more than 800 Colorado twins.

articles.title: Brain damage linked to “pseudopsychopathy” may not reduce the will to empathize
articles.summary: Since Phineas Gage, damage to the ventromedial prefrontal cortex has been linked to social indifference. A new lesion study suggests the willingness to empathize survives such injuries even when the execution does not.

articles.title: New research finds high testosterone does not impair men’s emotional reframing
articles.summary: Cortisol is often blamed for stress and testosterone for anger. Yet new research suggests higher resting cortisol may help practiced men reframe mild negative feelings, while testosterone levels showed no tie to emotional control.

articles.title: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary: A revolutionary new wearable patch could help people get more restorative sleep without medication or surgery. Developed by University of Texas researchers, the device uses gentle ultrasound to stimulate deep brain regions, helping participants enter REM sleep 43 minutes faster and remain there 16 minutes longer on average. The technology also showed promising effects on stress regulation and brain circuits involved in emotion.

articles.title: New study finds bosses who brag about their own good deeds risk disgusting their employees
articles.summary: A manager who talks about their own fairness and compassion can inspire employees or come across as self-righteous. New research across 254 workplace pairs and a controlled experiment suggests the difference lies in whether the boss also credits others.

articles.title: Psychedelics trigger a bizarre memory paradox that makes the unknown feel like home
articles.summary: Psychedelic trips feel strikingly new. Yet users often describe arriving somewhere they already know. A new study suggests this paradoxical familiarity differs from both everyday déjà vu and cherished personal memories.

articles.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. articles.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior.

articles.title: Check Token: Real-Time Self-Verification and Precise Truncation in LLM Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ECC memory embeds 8 parity bits for every 64 data bits and automatically detects and corrects errors on each read. The parity bits carry no data and only safeguard integrity, at ~12.5% overhead. Yet the reasoning chains of large language models lack such built-in self-verification: once an error occurs it propagates along the chain, and existing methods can only verify externally after generation completes. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data leakage is widely recognized as a threat to trustworthy machine-learning evaluation, yet the phrase covers mechanisms with very different statistical consequences.
